title: Enquirer’s Guide: Can I see the Stratum with my own eyes?
summary: One may see an apparatus, its shadow, and sometimes the appearance of an opening.
author: The Enquirer’s Guide Desk
paragraphs: This entry from The Enquirer’s Guide answers a question often put to the Society: “Can I see the Stratum with my own eyes?”
One may see an apparatus, its shadow, and sometimes the appearance of an opening.
Those sights alone do not show the whole Stratum. Much of what we know comes from recorded traces, probes, and comparisons between instruments.

Readers should treat the answer as an introduction rather than a final authority. Eidetic science in Alderwick is reported through measurements, disputed interpretations and careful revisions, and a respectable enquiry may properly end with further questions.
